267: /**
268:  * title -> { public_n, state, queue }, read once per pass.
269:  *
270:  * NOT from `bugctl create`. On the existing path create returns a stub: for a
271:  * card that was really #58 and in_fix it reported `public_n: 0`, `state: "new"`
272:  * and `queue: "ready"`, at both the top level and inside work_item. An
273:  * idempotent consumer that trusts that response re-packs a card an agent is
274:  * already working on, and `pack` overwrites the defect and resets the state —
275:  * which is exactly what un-blocks the dispatch guard for a second agent.
276:  *
277:  * So the state is read from the canonical list, once, and trusted over create.
278:  * Keyed by title because that is the only handle a page comment has: its
279:  * deterministic title_key.
280:  */
281: function bugIndex() {
282:   const r = bugctl(['list', '--json']);
283:   if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, why: r.err || `bugctl list exit ${r.code}` };
284:   let rows;
285:   try {
286:     rows = JSON.parse(r.out.slice(r.out.indexOf('{'))).rows;
287:   } catch (e) {
288:     return { ok: false, why: `could not read bugctl list: ${r.out.slice(0, 120)}` };
289:   }
290:   const map = new Map();
291:   for (const row of (rows || [])) {
292:     if (row && row.title) {
293:       map.set(row.title, {
294:         tag_id: row.tag_id || null,
295:         public_n: row.public_n || null,
296:         state: row.state || row.status || null,
297:         queue: row.queue || null,
298:       });
299:     }
300:   }
301:   return { ok: true, map };
302: }
303: 
304: /**
305:  * create -> pack -> dispatch. All three, in that order.
306:  *
307:  * `create` is idempotent by title_key, so re-running costs nothing. `pack` is the
308:  * one step that is NOT idempotent: POST /api/bugs/:id/defect overwrites item.defect
309:  * unconditionally. It is safe here only because `create` on an already-claimed
310:  * comment returns the EXISTING id and we skip straight to dispatch, whose own PID
311:  * lock refuses a second run.
312:  */
313: function fileAndDispatch(comment, parsed, slug, index) {
314:   const title = claimTitle(slug, comment.id);
315:   const known = index && index.ok ? index.map.get(title) || null : null;
316: 
317:   // THE CLAIM, and the reason this function is safe to run every five minutes.
318:   //
319:   // Read the card BEFORE creating anything. If it is already there and is past
320:   // `packed`, this comment has been dealt with: an agent is on it, or it is
321:   // awaiting verification, or it is done. Re-packing it would overwrite the
322:   // defect pack and reset the state, which is what lets the dispatch guard
323:   // admit a second agent for work already in flight.
324:   if (known) {
325:     return {
326:       stage: 'skip', ok: true, already: known.state,
327:       id: known.tag_id || null, publicN: known.public_n,
328:       why: `already ${known.state || 'filed'} — not re-filed`,
329:     };
330:   }
331: 
332:   const created = bugctl(['create', '--title', title, '--json']);
333:   if (!created.ok) return { stage: 'create', ...created };
334: 
335:   let id = null;
336:   try {
337:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
338:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
339:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
340:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
341:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
342:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
343:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
344:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
345:     : null;
346: 
347:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
348:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
349:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
350:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
351:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };
352: 
353:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
354:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
355:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
356:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
357:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
358:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
359:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
360:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
361:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
362:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
363:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
364:   const result = {
365:     stage: 'dispatch',
366:     id,
367:     publicN,
368:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
369:     code: dispatched.status,
370:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
371:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
372:   };
373:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
374:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
375:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
376:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
377:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
378:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
379:     result.notified = n.ok;
380:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
381:   }
382:   return result;
383: }

385: // ------------------------------------------------------- the notification path --
386: //
387: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
388: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
389: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
390: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
391: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
392: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
393: //
394: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
395: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
396: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
397: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
398: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
399: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.
400: //
401: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
402: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
403: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
404: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
405: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
406: // cannot set its own tag").
407: //
408: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
409: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
410: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
411: // back to plain text.
412: 
413: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
414: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';

416: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
417:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
418:  *  have to travel in the message. */
419: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
420:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
421:   const lines = [
422:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
423:     '',
424:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
425:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
426:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
427:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
428:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
429:     '',
430:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
431:     '',
432:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
433:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',
434:     'future instances inherit the fix. Do not patch the page fragment.',
435:   ];
436:   return lines.join('\n');
437: }

439: /**
440:  * Hand the instruction to @VM_19485_bot as a user message.
441:  *
442:  * Runs on the VM (where the user session lives). Returns the same shape as
443:  * fileAndDispatch so the caller does not care which path ran.
444:  */
445: function notifyVmBot(parsed, comment, slug) {
446:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
447:   const lib = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'lib', 'tg-userbot.mjs');
448:   if (!fs.existsSync(lib)) {
449:     return { stage: 'notify', ok: false, why: `no tg-userbot at ${lib} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
450:   }
451:   const chat = process.env.TG_CHAT_ID || TG_CHAT_DEFAULT;
452:   const mod = pathToFileURL(lib).href;
453:   const script = [
454:     `const m = await import(${JSON.stringify(mod)});`,
455:     `const s = await m.sendAsUser(${JSON.stringify(chat)}, ${JSON.stringify(botMessage(parsed, comment, slug))});`,
456:     `console.log(JSON.stringify(s && s.ok !== false ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, why: String(s) }));`,
457:   ].join('\n');
458: 
459:   const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', script],
460:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 120000 });
461:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
462:   const err = (r.stderr || '').trim();

475: /**
476:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
477:  *
478:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
479:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
480:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.
481:  *
482:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
483:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
484:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
485:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
486:  */
487: function escapeMd(s) {
488:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');
489: }

491: function notifyChat(lines) {
492:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
493:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
494:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
495:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
496: 
497:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
498:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
499:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
500:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
501:   //
502:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and
503:   // `ps` are world-readable, so the token belongs in a 0600 file rather than in
504:   // the unit or in the repository.
505:   const env = Object.assign({}, process.env);
506:   if (!env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) {
507:     const f = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_FILE;
508:     if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
509:       const m = /^\s*(?:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
510:       if (m) env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN = m[1];
511:     }
512:   }
513: 
514:   const r = spawnSync('bash', [sh, `--text=${text}`],
515:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, env });
516:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
517:   return {
518:     ok: r.status === 0,
519:     out: out.slice(-160),
520:     why: r.status === 0 ? null
521:       : ((r.stderr || '') + ' ' + out).trim().split('\n').pop().slice(0, 160),
522:   };
523: }

767: async function once(slug) {
768:   const cfg = supabaseConfig();
769:   if (!cfg.key) {
770:     console.error(`  cannot read comments: ${cfg.why || 'no Supabase key available'}`);
771:     process.exitCode = 1; return;
772:   }
773: 
774:   // REFUSE, DO NOT POLL. If threading is live and this is not a privileged key,
775:   // the read below returns [] whether or not there is work, and reporting "no
776:   // /bot comments" would be a lie that reads like good news.
777:   if (!cfg.privileged) {
778:     const probe = await probeThreading(cfg);
779:     if (probe.threaded) {
780:       console.error('  REFUSING TO POLL: threading is live and this key is not privileged.');
781:       console.error(`    the key in use is: ${cfg.keyKind}`);
782:       console.error('    20261014090000 narrowed page_comments SELECT to signed-in users.');
783:       console.error('    The publishable key now reads ZERO rows with NO error, so a poll here');
784:       console.error('    would report "no /bot comments" forever while dispatching nothing.');
785:       console.error('    Fix: set SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE to a 0600 file holding the');
786:       console.error('    project SECRET key (Dashboard -> Project Settings -> API Keys -> the');
787:       console.error('    sb_secret_ one, NOT the sb_publishable_ one shown beside it).');
788:       process.exitCode = 1;
789:       return;
790:     }
791:     console.log(`  using the ${cfg.keyKind} key — threading is not applied yet, so reads are still open`);
792:   }
793: 
794:   const got = await fetchBotComments(cfg, slug);
795:   if (got.error) { console.error(`  cannot read comments: ${got.error}`); process.exitCode = 1; return; }
796:   if (!got.rows.length) { console.log('  no /bot comments'); return; }
797:   console.log(`  ${got.rows.length} /bot comment(s)`);
798: 
799:   const notify = has('--notify');
800:   // One canonical read of the store per pass, so a comment already dealt with is
801:   // recognised as such instead of being re-packed and re-dispatched every tick.
802:   let index = { ok: false, map: new Map() };
803:   if (!notify) {
804:     index = bugIndex();
805:     if (!index.ok) { console.error(`  cannot read the bug store: ${index.why}`); process.exitCode = 1; return; }
806:   }
807:   let anyFail = false;
808:   for (const c of got.rows) {
809:     const parsed = parseBot(c.body);
810:     if (!parsed) { console.log(`  ${c.id.slice(0, 8)} not an instruction — skipped`); continue; }
811:     const r = notify ? notifyVmBot(parsed, c, slug) : fileAndDispatch(c, parsed, slug, index);
812:     if (!r.ok) anyFail = true;
813:     const okMark = r.ok ? (r.stage === 'skip' ? 'skip' : 'ok  ') : 'FAIL';
814:     const card = ' ' + cardLabel(r.publicN, r.id);
815:     // The notify verdict is printed, never just recorded. result.notified was
816:     // set and never read, which meant a notice that failed to send looked

401: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
402: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
403: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
404: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
405: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
406: // cannot set its own tag").
407: //
408: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
409: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
410: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
411: // back to plain text.

413: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
414: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';

416: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
417:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
418:  *  have to travel in the message. */
419: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
420:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
421:   const lines = [
422:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
423:     '',
424:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
425:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
426:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
427:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
428:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
429:     '',
430:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
431:     '',
432:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
433:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',
434:     'future instances inherit the fix. Do not patch the page fragment.',
435:   ];
436:   return lines.join('\n');
437: }

439: /**
440:  * Hand the instruction to @VM_19485_bot as a user message.
441:  *
442:  * Runs on the VM (where the user session lives). Returns the same shape as
443:  * fileAndDispatch so the caller does not care which path ran.
444:  */
445: function notifyVmBot(parsed, comment, slug) {
446:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
447:   const lib = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'lib', 'tg-userbot.mjs');
448:   if (!fs.existsSync(lib)) {
449:     return { stage: 'notify', ok: false, why: `no tg-userbot at ${lib} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
450:   }
451:   const chat = process.env.TG_CHAT_ID || TG_CHAT_DEFAULT;
452:   const mod = pathToFileURL(lib).href;
453:   const script = [
454:     `const m = await import(${JSON.stringify(mod)});`,
455:     `const s = await m.sendAsUser(${JSON.stringify(chat)}, ${JSON.stringify(botMessage(parsed, comment, slug))});`,
456:     `console.log(JSON.stringify(s && s.ok !== false ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, why: String(s) }));`,
457:   ].join('\n');
458: 
459:   const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', script],
460:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 120000 });
461:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
462:   const err = (r.stderr || '').trim();
463:   try {
464:     const j = JSON.parse(out.slice(out.indexOf('{')));
465:     if (j.ok) return { stage: 'notify', ok: true, to: `@${VM_BOT_USERNAME}`, chat };
466:     return { stage: 'notify', ok: false, why: j.why || out.slice(0, 200) };
467:   } catch (e) {
468:     return {
469:       stage: 'notify', ok: false,
470:       why: err.slice(0, 200) || `exit ${r.status}: ${out.slice(0, 160)}`,
471:     };
472:   }
473: }

475: /**
476:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
477:  *
478:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
479:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
480:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.
481:  *
482:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
483:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
484:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
485:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
486:  */
487: function escapeMd(s) {
488:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');
489: }
490: 
491: function notifyChat(lines) {
492:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
493:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
494:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
495:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
496: 
497:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
498:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
499:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
500:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
501:   //
502:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and
503:   // `ps` are world-readable, so the token belongs in a 0600 file rather than in
504:   // the unit or in the repository.
505:   const env = Object.assign({}, process.env);
506:   if (!env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) {
507:     const f = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_FILE;
508:     if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
509:       const m = /^\s*(?:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
510:       if (m) env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN = m[1];
511:     }
512:   }
513: 
514:   const r = spawnSync('bash', [sh, `--text=${text}`],
515:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, env });
516:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
517:   return {
518:     ok: r.status === 0,
519:     out: out.slice(-160),
520:     why: r.status === 0 ? null
521:       : ((r.stderr || '') + ' ' + out).trim().split('\n').pop().slice(0, 160),
522:   };
523: }

534: /** The post-dispatch notice. Says what happened, where, and what to look at —

546:     `anchor: ${comment.anchor || 'none (unanchored comment)'}`,
547:     `ask:    ${parsed.instruction}`,
548:     '',
549:     state,
550:   ].join('\n');
551: }

335:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
336:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
337:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
338:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
339:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
340:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
341:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
342:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
343:     : null;

345:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
346:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
347:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
348:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
349:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };

351:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
352:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
353:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
354:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
355:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
356:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
357:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
358:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
359:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
360:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
361:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
362:   const result = {
363:     stage: 'dispatch',
364:     id,
365:     publicN,
366:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
367:     code: dispatched.status,
368:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
369:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
370:   };
371:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
372:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
373:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
374:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
375:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
376:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
377:     result.notified = n.ok;
378:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
379:   }
380:   return result;

383: // ------------------------------------------------------- the notification path --
384: //
385: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
386: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
387: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
388: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
389: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
390: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
391: //
392: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
393: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
394: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
395: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
396: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
397: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.
398: //
399: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
400: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
401: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
402: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
403: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
404: // cannot set its own tag").
405: //
406: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
407: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
408: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
409: // back to plain text.
410: 
411: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
412: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';
413: 
414: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
415:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
416:  *  have to travel in the message. */
417: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
418:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
419:   const lines = [
420:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
421:     '',
422:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
423:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
424:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
425:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
426:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
427:     '',
428:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
429:     '',
430:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
431:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',
432:     'future instances inherit the fix. Do not patch the page fragment.',
433:   ];
434:   return lines.join('\n');
435: }

437: /**
438:  * Hand the instruction to @VM_19485_bot as a user message.
439:  *
440:  * Runs on the VM (where the user session lives). Returns the same shape as
441:  * fileAndDispatch so the caller does not care which path ran.
442:  */
443: function notifyVmBot(parsed, comment, slug) {
444:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
445:   const lib = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'lib', 'tg-userbot.mjs');
446:   if (!fs.existsSync(lib)) {
447:     return { stage: 'notify', ok: false, why: `no tg-userbot at ${lib} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
448:   }
449:   const chat = process.env.TG_CHAT_ID || TG_CHAT_DEFAULT;
450:   const mod = pathToFileURL(lib).href;
451:   const script = [
452:     `const m = await import(${JSON.stringify(mod)});`,
453:     `const s = await m.sendAsUser(${JSON.stringify(chat)}, ${JSON.stringify(botMessage(parsed, comment, slug))});`,
454:     `console.log(JSON.stringify(s && s.ok !== false ? { ok: true } : { ok: false, why: String(s) }));`,
455:   ].join('\n');
456: 
457:   const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', script],
458:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 120000 });
459:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
460:   const err = (r.stderr || '').trim();
461:   try {
462:     const j = JSON.parse(out.slice(out.indexOf('{')));
463:     if (j.ok) return { stage: 'notify', ok: true, to: `@${VM_BOT_USERNAME}`, chat };
464:     return { stage: 'notify', ok: false, why: j.why || out.slice(0, 200) };
465:   } catch (e) {
466:     return {
467:       stage: 'notify', ok: false,
468:       why: err.slice(0, 200) || `exit ${r.status}: ${out.slice(0, 160)}`,
469:     };
470:   }
471: }

473: /**
474:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
475:  *
476:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
477:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
478:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.
479:  *
480:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
481:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
482:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
483:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
484:  */
485: function escapeMd(s) {
486:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');
487: }
488: 
489: function notifyChat(lines) {
490:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
491:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
492:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
493:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
494: 
495:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
496:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
497:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
498:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
499:   //
500:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and
501:   // `ps` are world-readable, so the token belongs in a 0600 file rather than in
502:   // the unit or in the repository.
503:   const env = Object.assign({}, process.env);
504:   if (!env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) {
505:     const f = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_FILE;
506:     if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
507:       const m = /^\s*(?:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
508:       if (m) env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN = m[1];
509:     }
510:   }
511: 
512:   const r = spawnSync('bash', [sh, `--text=${text}`],
513:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, env });
514:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
515:   return {
516:     ok: r.status === 0,
517:     out: out.slice(-160),
518:     why: r.status === 0 ? null
519:       : ((r.stderr || '') + ' ' + out).trim().split('\n').pop().slice(0, 160),
520:   };
521: }

523: /** What a human is shown for a card.
524:  *
525:  *  tag_id is what `--id` needs; public_n is what a human needs. Showing someone
526:  *  "card #tag_mv83i63b_mdu16v" is not a notification, it is a riddle. The public
527:  *  number wins whenever create reported one, which it always does. */
528: function cardLabel(publicN, id) {
529:   return publicN ? '#' + publicN : String(id || '?');
530: }

532: /** The post-dispatch notice. Says what happened, where, and what to look at —
533:  *  a notification that does not name the card is not one. */
534: function filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, dispatched, detached) {
535:   const state = !dispatched.ok
536:     ? 'Dispatch did not exit clean — the card is packed and queued, but nothing started on its own.'
537:     : detached
538:       ? 'Dispatched detached: the agent was launched and will push from its own worktree. This card is the thing to watch — it is the only proof the work finished.'
539:       : 'Dispatched in the foreground. The agent works in its own worktree; watch the card for the commit.';
540:   return [
541:     `sage-prototypes: /bot filed as card #${card}`,
542:     '',
543:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}`,
544:     `anchor: ${comment.anchor || 'none (unanchored comment)'}`,
545:     `ask:    ${parsed.instruction}`,
546:     '',
547:     state,
548:   ].join('\n');
549: }

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // /bot poller — hands a page comment to a Health-tracker agent.
3: //
4: // WHY A POLLER AND NOT A WEBHOOK
5: // A webhook needs a public endpoint, and this site is static: vercel.json has no
6: // functions and AGENTS.md forbids adding a build step. So a browser cannot push
7: // anywhere. It writes the comment (which it already can) and something with
8: // outbound access comes and gets it. The same reasoning as sync-watch.js, which
9: // polls Figma for the same reason.
10: //
11: // WHERE IT RUNS
12: // On the VM, beside the bots. SSH as ubuntu@51.254.217.163 works and ~/bot-host is
13: // the Health-tracker checkout. It also runs here read-only against the same REST
14: // endpoint, which is how it is tested.
15: //
16: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --once      poll once
17: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --watch     poll every --interval seconds
18: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --selftest  offline, no network
19: //
20: //   add --notify to hand the instruction to the VM bot over Telegram instead of
21: //   filing the card here. See "the notification path" below for why that is the
22: //   default shape to grow toward: it needs no credential off-box, and a human
23: //   sees the instruction. Without --notify this file still does create -> pack ->
24: //   dispatch itself, which is the right thing when it runs beside the bots.
25: //
26: // THE CLAIM IS ATOMIC, AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE
27: // Filing the card is what claims the comment. POST /api/bugs dedupes on title_key,
28: // so `page:<slug> comment:<uuid>` returns 200 {existing:true} for a comment already
29: // filed and creates nothing. That is an atomic conditional write at the store,
30: // which is the whole point of the Idempotent Consumer pattern: a check-then-set in
31: // a poller has a window where two overlapping passes both pass the check.
32: //
33: // The claim is atomic, and it is not in this file. Filing the card is what claims
34: // the comment: the store dedupes on title_key, so `page:<slug> comment:<uuid>`
35: // returns the existing card and creates nothing. That is an atomic conditional
36: // write at the store, which is the whole point of the Idempotent Consumer pattern:
37: // a check-then-set in a poller has a window where two overlapping passes both
38: // pass the check.
39: //
40: //   What I had wrong, and what this now says instead: "create is idempotent" was
41: //   true and useless on its own. `pack` overwrites the defect pack and resets the
42: //   card's state unconditionally, and it is the reset that re-opens the dispatch
43: //   guard — so a poller that re-created and re-packed every recent comment would
44: //   have unblocked a SECOND agent on work already in flight, every five minutes.
45: //   So the store is read once per pass (bugIndex) and a comment whose card is
46: //   already past `packed` is skipped, not re-packed. The card is the record; the
47: //   poller reads it rather than keeping a state file of its own.
48: //
49: //   The trap: `create` alone is not dispatch. run-coding-dispatch.sh --task= is
50: //   refused by packCheck (exit 1) for an unpacked card, and --ticket= refuses a
51: //   card with no defect (exit 3). All four of pack's fields are mandatory.
52: //
53: //   create's RESPONSE is not trustworthy on the existing path: it reports
54: //   public_n 0 and state "new" for a card that is really #58 and in_fix. Only
55: //   bugctl list is believed. That is a bugctl defect, filed as its own card.

58: const fs = require('fs');
59: const path = require('path');

69: // -------------------------------------------------------------- the parser --
70: //
71: // MUST match components/page-comments.js parseBot. They drifted once and the
72: // panel announced one agent while the dispatcher posted to another. An `@` is
73: // required before a target, because an optional bare word is greedy: "/bot fix
74: // the second card" would parse target="fix" and eat the first word of every
75: // multi-word instruction.
76: function parseBot(body) {
77:   const text = body || '';
78:   const m = /^\s*\/bot(?:\s+@([a-z0-9_-]+))?\s+([\s\S]+)$/i.exec(text);
79:   if (!m) return null;
80:   if (!m[1] && /^\s*\/bot\s+@/i.test(text)) return null;
81:   return { target: m[1] || null, instruction: m[2].trim() };
82: }
83: 
84: /**
85:  * The deterministic title that IS the claim.
86:  *
87:  * Two runs of this poller over the same comment produce the same title_key, so the
88:  * second is refused by the store rather than by anything in this process. It must
89:  * not contain the instruction: the instruction changes if someone edits the
90:  * comment, and an edit must not become a second claim.
91:  */
92: function claimTitle(slug, commentId) {
93:   return `page:${slug} comment:${commentId}`;
94: }
95: 
96: /** Pack's four fields are mandatory and the dispatcher refuses a card without
97:  *  them, so they are derived rather than left to an operator. */
98: function packFields(parsed, anchor, slug) {
99:   const where = anchor ? anchor.replace(/^component:/, '') : 'an unanchored element';
100:   return {
101:     component: where,
102:     observed: `A reviewer left a comment on the ${slug} page, anchored to ${where}.`,
103:     expected: parsed.instruction,
104:     criteria:
105:       'Make the change in the component named above only. Run node tooling/sync-check.js '
106:       + 'and node tooling/render-check.js, then commit. Report the result back on the '
107:       + 'comment thread.',
108:   };
109: }

111: // -------------------------------------------------------------- the plumbing --
112: /**
113:  * Where the poller reads from.
114:  *
115:  * The page's key is a Supabase *publishable* key — it is in the page on purpose,
116:  * and it is what the browser uses. Reading it from the same place the browser
117:  * does means a machine with the repo cloned can poll with nothing configured, and
118:  * there is no second copy of a credential to go stale.
119:  *
120:  * That only works while `page_comments` is public-read. It is not, and will not
121:  * be: 20261014090000 narrows SELECT to `auth.uid() is not null`, which is the
122:  * stated requirement — sign-in gates the panel for read AND write — and a
123:  * client-side gate is not a gate.
124:  *
125:  * So the poller needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS. The publishable
126:  * key is still the default for a reason worth keeping: it is the one that works
127:  * without a secret, and probeThreading() below is what stops it being used once it
128:  * stops working. See there for why "zero rows and no error" is the most dangerous
129:  * possible outcome for a poller.
130:  *
131:  * SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE is preferred over the bare variable so the key
132:  * never appears in `systemctl cat`, `ps`, or a unit file in the repo.
133:  */
134: /**
135:  * Is this key actually privileged? A FILE RESOLVING IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION.
136:  *
137:  * This exists because the first version of the guard checked only whether
138:  * SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE had produced a string, and the publishable key
139:  * was pasted into that file by mistake. It is the same length, it is the same
140:  * value that sits in the page HTML, and the poller went green and reported "no
141:  * /bot comments" — the exact silent failure the guard was written to stop. A
142:  * guard that can be satisfied by the wrong credential is not a guard.
143:  *
144:  * So the key itself is inspected, and an unrecognised shape fails CLOSED:
145:  *
146:  *   sb_secret_…      privileged
147:  *   sb_publishable_…  NOT privileged, by definition
148:  *   eyJ…             a legacy JWT: decode the payload and read its `role`.
149:  *                     anon is not service_role, and saying so beats guessing.
150:  *   anything else    not privileged
151:  */
152: function isPrivilegedKey(k) {
153:   if (!k) return false;
154:   if (k.startsWith('sb_publishable_')) return false;
155:   if (k.startsWith('sb_secret_')) return true;
156:   if (k.startsWith('eyJ')) {
157:     try {
158:       const payload = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(k.split('.')[1], 'base64').toString('utf8'));
159:       return payload.role === 'service_role';
160:     } catch (e) { return false; }
161:   }
162:   return false;
163: }

165: function supabaseConfig() {
166:   let pageKey = null, pageUrl = null;
167:   try {
168:     const html = fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'ongoing_project', 'cpp', DEFAULT_PAGE, 'index.html'), 'utf8');
169:     pageKey = (/data-supabase-anon-key="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
170:     pageUrl = (/data-supabase-url="([^"]+)"/.exec(html) || [])[1] || null;
171:   } catch (e) { /* no page to read; env may still carry it */ }
172: 
173:   // Read the secret from a file when one is named, so it never lands in a unit
174:   // file, in `ps`, or in `systemctl cat`. A 0600 file owned by ubuntu is a
175:   // smaller thing to get wrong than an environment variable in a committed
176:   // workflow.
177:   let fileKey = null;
178:   const keyFile = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE;
179:   if (keyFile) {
180:     try {
181:       const raw = fs.readFileSync(keyFile, 'utf8').trim();
182:       // Accept either a bare key or KEY=value, because both shapes are in the
183:       // wild and a file that silently yields '' is worse than no file at all.
184:       const m = /^\s*(?:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(raw);
185:       fileKey = m ? m[1] : null;
186:     } catch (e) {
187:       if (process.env.SUPABASE_REQUIRE_SECRET === '1') {
188:         return { url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl, key: null, why: `cannot read SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE at ${keyFile}: ${e.message}` };
189:       }
190:     }
191:   }
192: 
193:   const privileged = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY || fileKey;
194:   const secret = privileged || process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY || pageKey;
195:   return {
196:     url: process.env.SUPABASE_URL || pageUrl || 'https://ltyyzxnxufvkorekglrf.supabase.co',
197:     key: secret,
198:     // What the key IS, not where it came from. A file resolving tells you
199:     // nothing about what is in it, and the publishable key resolved from a
200:     // perfectly readable 0600 file.
201:     privileged: isPrivilegedKey(privileged),
202:     keyKind: privileged
203:       ? (isPrivilegedKey(privileged) ? 'service_role' : 'not-privileged')
204:       : (isPrivilegedKey(secret) ? 'service_role' : 'publishable'),
205:   };
206: }

208: /**
209:  * Has the threading migration been applied?
210:  *
211:  * THIS EXISTS BECAUSE OF THE WORST POSSIBLE POLLER FAILURE.
212:  *
213:  * `select id from page_comments limit 1` returns `[]` both when the table is
214:  * genuinely empty and when RLS is hiding every row from this key. There is no
215:  * error, no status code, no warning. So once 20261014090000 narrows SELECT to
216:  * signed-in users, a poller still holding the publishable key reads "no /bot
217:  * comments" forever, exits 0, and stops dispatching — with nothing anywhere
218:  * saying why. The timer would look perfectly healthy.
219:  *
220:  * `parent_id` exists if and only if that migration ran, and selecting a column
221:  * that does not exist is a hard 400 rather than an empty array. That asymmetry
222:  * is the only thing that distinguishes "nothing to do" from "you cannot see
223:  * anything", and it is the only reason this function exists.
224:  */
225: async function probeThreading(cfg) {
226:   if (!cfg.key) return { threaded: false, why: 'no key' };
227:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?select=parent_id&limit=1`;
228:   try {
229:     const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
230:     if (res.status === 400) return { threaded: false }; // column absent -> not applied
231:     if (!res.ok) return { threaded: false, why: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
232:     return { threaded: true };
233:   } catch (e) {
234:     return { threaded: false, why: e.message };
235:   }
236: }
237: 
238: async function fetchBotComments(cfg, slug) {
239:   if (!cfg.key) return { error: 'no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or ANON_KEY) in the environment' };
240:   const q = new URLSearchParams({
241:     select: 'id, body, anchor, created_at',
242:     page_slug: `eq.${slug}`,
243:     order: 'created_at.desc',
244:     limit: '25',
245:   });
246:   // body is filtered by the partial index page_comments_bot_body_idx. The
247:   // supabase-js query builder cannot express `like`, so this is a raw fetch.
248:   const url = `${cfg.url}/rest/v1/page_comments?${q}&body=like.%2Fbot%25`;
249:   const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { apikey: cfg.key, Authorization: `Bearer ${cfg.key}` } });
250:   if (!res.ok) return { error: `HTTP ${res.status} — ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 160)}` };
251:   const rows = await res.json();
252:   return { rows: Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : [] };
253: }
254: 
255: function bugctl(args, opts = {}) {
256:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
257:   if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'))) {
258:     return { ok: false, why: `no bugctl at ${repo} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
259:   }
260:   const r = spawnSync('node', [path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'bugctl.mjs'), ...args],
261:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, ...opts });
262:   return { ok: r.status === 0, code: r.status, out: (r.stdout || '').trim(), err: (r.stderr || '').trim() };
263: }
264: 
265: /**
266:  * title -> { public_n, state, queue }, read once per pass.
267:  *
268:  * NOT from `bugctl create`. On the existing path create returns a stub: for a
269:  * card that was really #58 and in_fix it reported `public_n: 0`, `state: "new"`
270:  * and `queue: "ready"`, at both the top level and inside work_item. An
271:  * idempotent consumer that trusts that response re-packs a card an agent is
272:  * already working on, and `pack` overwrites the defect and resets the state —
273:  * which is exactly what un-blocks the dispatch guard for a second agent.
274:  *
275:  * So the state is read from the canonical list, once, and trusted over create.
276:  * Keyed by title because that is the only handle a page comment has: its
277:  * deterministic title_key.
278:  */
279: function bugIndex() {
280:   const r = bugctl(['list', '--json']);
281:   if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, why: r.err || `bugctl list exit ${r.code}` };
282:   let rows;
283:   try {
284:     rows = JSON.parse(r.out.slice(r.out.indexOf('{'))).rows;
285:   } catch (e) {
286:     return { ok: false, why: `could not read bugctl list: ${r.out.slice(0, 120)}` };
287:   }
288:   const map = new Map();
289:   for (const row of (rows || [])) {
290:     if (row && row.title) {
291:       map.set(row.title, {
292:         tag_id: row.tag_id || null,
293:         public_n: row.public_n || null,
294:         state: row.state || row.status || null,
295:         queue: row.queue || null,
296:       });
297:     }
298:   }
299:   return { ok: true, map };
300: }
301: 
302: /**
303:  * create -> pack -> dispatch. All three, in that order.
304:  *
305:  * `create` is idempotent by title_key, so re-running costs nothing. `pack` is the
306:  * one step that is NOT idempotent: POST /api/bugs/:id/defect overwrites item.defect
307:  * unconditionally. It is safe here only because `create` on an already-claimed
308:  * comment returns the EXISTING id and we skip straight to dispatch, whose own PID
309:  * lock refuses a second run.
310:  */
311: function fileAndDispatch(comment, parsed, slug, index) {
312:   const title = claimTitle(slug, comment.id);
313:   const known = index && index.ok ? index.map.get(title) || null : null;
314: 
315:   // THE CLAIM, and the reason this function is safe to run every five minutes.
316:   //
317:   // Read the card BEFORE creating anything. If it is already there and is past
318:   // `packed`, this comment has been dealt with: an agent is on it, or it is
319:   // awaiting verification, or it is done. Re-packing it would overwrite the
320:   // defect pack and reset the state, which is what lets the dispatch guard
321:   // admit a second agent for work already in flight.
322:   if (known) {
323:     return {
324:       stage: 'skip', ok: true, already: known.state,
325:       id: known.tag_id || null, publicN: known.public_n,
326:       why: `already ${known.state || 'filed'} — not re-filed`,
327:     };
328:   }
329: 
330:   const created = bugctl(['create', '--title', title, '--json']);
331:   if (!created.ok) return { stage: 'create', ...created };
332: 
333:   let id = null;
334:   try {
335:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
336:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
337:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
338:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
339:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
340:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
341:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
342:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
343:     : null;
344: 
345:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
346:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
347:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
348:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
349:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };
350: 
351:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
352:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
353:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
354:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
355:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
356:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
357:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
358:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
359:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
360:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
361:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
362:   const result = {
363:     stage: 'dispatch',
364:     id,
365:     publicN,
366:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
367:     code: dispatched.status,
368:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
369:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
370:   };
371:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
372:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
373:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
374:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
375:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
376:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
377:     result.notified = n.ok;
378:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
379:   }
380:   return result;
381: }
382: 
383: // ------------------------------------------------------- the notification path --
384: //
385: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
386: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
387: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
388: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
389: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
390: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
391: //
392: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
393: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
394: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
395: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
396: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
397: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.
398: //
399: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT
400: // Telegram never delivers a bot's own sendMessage back to it. Sending as
401: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
402: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
403: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot
404: // cannot set its own tag").
405: //
406: // sendAsUser sets no parse_mode, so none of this is Markdown: identifiers with
407: // underscores (page_comments, customer_payment) reach the bot intact. The
408: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell
409: // back to plain text.

411: const VM_BOT_USERNAME = 'VM_19485_bot';
412: const TG_CHAT_DEFAULT = '6218257274';

414: /** The text the VM bot receives. Self-contained: its agent has Health-tracker's
415:  *  context, not sage-prototypes', so the page, the anchor and the comment id all
416:  *  have to travel in the message. */
417: function botMessage(parsed, comment, slug) {
418:   const anchor = comment.anchor ? String(comment.anchor) : 'none (unanchored comment)';
419:   const lines = [
420:     'A /bot instruction arrived on the sage-prototypes site.',
421:     '',
422:     `repo:   /home/ubuntu/src/work/sage-prototypes`,
423:     `page:   ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}   (live: https://sage-prototypes.vercel.app/ongoing_project/cpp/${slug}/)`,
424:     `anchor: ${anchor}`,
425:     `comment id: ${comment.id}`,
426:     parsed.target ? `target agent: @${parsed.target}` : 'target agent: none named — you were chosen as the default',
427:     '',
428:     `instruction: ${parsed.instruction}`,
429:     '',
430:     'File it as a bug card (bugctl create --title "page:' + slug + ' comment:' + comment.id + '"',
431:     'then pack all four fields, then dispatch), then work it at COMPONENT level so',
432:     'future instances inherit the fix. Do not patch the page fragment.',
433:   ];
434:   return lines.join('\n');
435: }

437: /**
438:  * Hand the instruction to @VM_19485_bot as a user message.
439:  *
440:  * Runs on the VM (where the user session lives). Returns the same shape as
441:  * fileAndDispatch so the caller does not care which path ran.
442:  */
443: function notifyVmBot(parsed, comment, slug) {
444:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
445:   const lib = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'lib', 'tg-userbot.mjs');
446:   if (!fs.existsSync(lib)) {

473: /**
474:  * Tell the human, over Telegram, that a card exists.
475:  *
476:  * This is the part that works with nothing provisioned. telegram-send.sh already
477:  * sends as the live bot token and the delivery is verified; it needs no user
478:  * session, no teleproto and no credential off the box.
479:  *
480:  * telegram-send.sh hardcodes parse_mode=Markdown and has no flag to turn it off,
481:  * so any message with two underscores fails once and retries as plain text. The
482:  * retry is invisible but the failed call is not, so Markdown-active characters
483:  * are escaped here rather than paying for a round trip every time.
484:  */
485: function escapeMd(s) {
486:   return s.replace(/([_*`[\]])/g, '\\$1');
487: }

489: function notifyChat(lines) {
490:   const repo = process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker');
491:   const sh = path.join(repo, 'scripts', 'telegram-send.sh');
492:   if (!fs.existsSync(sh)) return { ok: false, why: `no telegram-send.sh at ${sh} (set BOT_HOST_DIR)` };
493:   const text = escapeMd(String(lines).trim());
494: 
495:   // Pin the sender. Without this, telegram-send.sh falls back to ~/.hermes/.env
496:   // and every comment arrived from @Health_tracker_159bot, while deploy and push
497:   // notifications came from @VM_19485_bot — two bots, one system, and no way to
498:   // tell at a glance which notification you were looking at.
499:   //
500:   // Read from a file for the same reason as the Supabase key: `systemctl cat` and
501:   // `ps` are world-readable, so the token belongs in a 0600 file rather than in
502:   // the unit or in the repository.
503:   const env = Object.assign({}, process.env);
504:   if (!env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN) {
505:     const f = process.env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_FILE;
506:     if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
507:       const m = /^\s*(?:TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
508:       if (m) env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN = m[1];
509:     }
510:   }
511: 
512:   const r = spawnSync('bash', [sh, `--text=${text}`],
513:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: repo, timeout: 60000, env });
514:   const out = (r.stdout || '').trim();
515:   return {
516:     ok: r.status === 0,
517:     out: out.slice(-160),
518:     why: r.status === 0 ? null
519:       : ((r.stderr || '') + ' ' + out).trim().split('\n').pop().slice(0, 160),
520:   };
